newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen lacking clear direction vs yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen lacking clear direction vs yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be directionless against the yen in Asia on Tuesday, with activity mainly driven by movements of the mark, dealers said.
Although the dollar recovered to 118 yen overnight, traders in Tokyo could be reluctant to keep buying dollars above 118 yen due to fears of a sudden fall, as occurred last week.

"It will be directionless," said a trust bank dealer. "Although the dollar's downside could be limited, there is caution about testing the upside actively due to fears of a sudden fall," he added. The first resistance is seen at 118.30 yen and then at 118.50 yen, he said.

Dealers said some dollars at 118.50 yen, but their sales would not be very aggressive. Another trust bank dealer said the dollar/yen rate had lacked energy to move on its own, and direction was likely to be set by activity by overseas fund operators.
"The dollar/yen rate will be all up to overseas funds," he added. But he said lingering mark selling interest against the yen may indirectly put downward pressure on the yen.
The dollar rose against the mark and yen on Monday in New York, buoyed by an impressive turnaround in U.S. stocks and remarks by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp.
